_source: Copied verbatim from the brain Workbench (plan 2026-11-16-workbench-ad-manager, decision 9). Cards, base, standupPrompt, setupPrompts and actionLabels: tools/members/command-centre/public/ads-command-board.html (TYPES, COLS, BASE, TASKS, CONTRACT_PATH, P_DISCOVER, P_SHEET, P_PROXY, STANDUP_PROMPT, ACTION_LABELS). revisePrompt: tools/members/command-centre/server.cjs (POST /api/approvals/decide), with its ${...} parts written as {{id}}, {{client}}, {{name}} and {{note}} (the note with double quotes turned into single ones). draftChangePrompt: the same file (POST /api/approvals/decided, the draftChange prompt), written the same way. Each card prompt is BASE plus its own text, as the board builds it. {{account}} is the account name and {{key}} the account key. Never edit by hand: copy again from the source and update SOURCES.md.

insight.label: Insight

base: You are managing the Google Ads account {{account}}. The board's quick-view CSVs for this account are in clients/{{key}}/context/google-ads/board/ — summary.csv (per-campaign DAILY rows, ~last 45 days), search80.csv (search terms), keyword80.csv, productID.csv (shopping products) and quality.csv. The fuller Google Ads export (assets, budgets, settings, negatives, etc.) is in clients/{{key}}/context/google-ads/data/ but may be older. The brain root is your working directory. Always check what's actually present before relying on a file; if what you need is missing or stale, pull it fresh via the gads-proxy (.claude/skills/gads-proxy/scripts/query.cjs) or the gads-context skill. Treat conversion/CPA figures cautiously — if they look wildly off versus spend, suspect a tracking/attribution artefact and flag it rather than trusting it.

Treat conversion/CPA figures cautiously — if they look wildly off versus spend, suspect a tracking/attribution artefact and flag it rather than trusting it. Using summary.csv (per-campaign daily rows), compare yesterday — the latest date in the file — against the trailing 30-day average for spend, conversions and CPA per campaign. Flag anything more than 25% off baseline. If summary.csv doesn't cover enough days for a real baseline, pull a fresh daily campaign series via the proxy first. Write a 5-line plain-English summary of what moved and whether any of it needs a human eye.

standupPrompt: You are running the Daily Standup for the Google Ads account {{account}} (the folder clients/{{key}}/). Follow .claude/skills/standup/SKILL.md exactly for account "{{key}}": run the config-drift guard first, then the deterministic analysts, narrate the ones that speak up, run the full bull/bear debate, the strategist synthesis, the constraint check and the account-director final call, then render the brief (render_brief.py then render_html.py --client {{key}}). The finished brief.html — headline, per-campaign verdicts, the debate transcript and the anomalies — is your result; it lands at clients/{{key}}/standup/<today>/brief.html. It is READ-ONLY: never change the account. The brain root is your working directory.

setupPrompts.discover: Look at how my Google Ads data is collected and get my Ads Command Board fully lit up. First, an important thing to know: the board reads TOLERANTLY. It accepts the clean 8020-script headers, raw proxy or API output (snake_case columns like metrics.cost_micros, cost in micros), and common filename variants, and it maps them all itself. So you do NOT need to rename columns, convert micros, or reshape anything by hand — landing the data is enough. Read the data contract at .claude/skills/workbench/assets/ads-data-contract.md for the list of datasets and where they live, then investigate what I already have: Google Sheets from the 8020 script, a Google Ads proxy (gads-proxy.yaml or GADS_PROXY_URL), a google-ads.yaml, or existing CSVs in my client data folders. Tell me in plain English what you found per account. Then set up the simplest reliable path that lands each dataset in the account's data folder in whatever shape it naturally comes out, run it once now so I can see the board light up. Then, BEFORE scheduling anything, check whether this account is already being fed on a schedule (an existing chore, launchd job, scheduled task, or daily refresh writing into this data folder) — if it is, leave it alone or update that one, do NOT stand up a second feed on top of it. Only add a new daily refresh if nothing is feeding it yet. Never fabricate data — if a dataset genuinely isn't available (for example no Shopping data on a lead-gen account), skip it and say so. Finish with a table of dataset, status, and source.
setupPrompts.sheet: My Google Ads data lives in Google Sheets written by the 8020 script. Read the data contract at .claude/skills/workbench/assets/ads-data-contract.md for the list of datasets, then find my sheet URL(s) — check my brain's configs first and ask me if you can't find them. For each account, download every tab into that account's data folder as a CSV. The 8020 tabs already line up with what the board reads, and the board maps headers tolerantly, so keep the tab names as the filenames and don't fuss over tweaking columns — it reads them as they are. Run it once now so I can see the board light up. Before scheduling a daily refresh, check whether this account is already being fed on a schedule — if it is, update that one rather than adding a second. If a tab doesn't exist in my sheet, skip it and list it at the end.
setupPrompts.proxy: I have the Google Ads proxy set up in my brain. Use the gads-proxy skill's query.cjs runner to fetch each dataset (read the data contract at .claude/skills/workbench/assets/ads-data-contract.md for the list) and write it STRAIGHT into the account's data folder. You do NOT need to rename columns or convert anything: the board reads the proxy's raw output directly, mapping the API's snake_case headers and converting cost out of micros itself. Use the contract's filenames where it's easy, but the board also recognises common variants. Run it once now so I can see the board light up. Before scheduling a daily refresh, check whether this account is already being fed on a schedule — if it is, update that one rather than adding a second. If a dataset genuinely isn't available (for example no Shopping data on a lead-gen account), skip it and say so at the end.
